_comment: Pins that reproduce public/dictionaries/wetext-*-tn-*.bin.zst byte for byte. Determined 2026-11-15 for the grammar-ownership PoC; see docs/superpowers/REPORT.md for the evidence behind each field and docs/superpowers/env.md / Dockerfile for the two working environments. The assets under public/dictionaries/ are generated from these pins and are NOT committed, so they must be rebuilt from this file — never hand-edited, and never treated as the source of truth.

upstream.note: The git submodule is the source of truth for the grammar code; the Docker image copies this checkout instead of cloning. The commit is the same one recorded under wetextprocessing below (kept there for its provenance note).

hashes._comment: wheel_parity_before_rules / wheel_parity_zstd_before_rules are historical: they are the output before any local rule, and are kept only as the PoC record. They are NOT a live baseline and `verify.py --mode parity` will not match once a local rule exists. assets / assets_zstd are the live baseline and the only one CI asserts. Byte identity is not required for correctness — see the conda-forge variant in docs/superpowers/REPORT.md — but it is what CI asserts.
hashes._outputs_note: `assets` is the amd64 build of the grammar we own (Roman key-word rule; money with cents and the symbols upstream does not read; `Cardinal.build_tagger` with the 1,000-1,999 weight sign flipped, so `1,234` reads "one thousand two hundred and thirty four"; English versions, the `24/7` idiom and `§` against its section number; digit-by-digit Japanese telephone and postal codes; Chinese thousands separators; and the fixes found in review: zero components in versions, postal only with `〒`, vulgar fractions in the gate, currency beside a grouped number through upstream's `money` token, and Roman key words cut back to proper names). A five-component bare dot chain is still split by the three-component version rule; covering it means looping the cardinal word graph, which the build cannot afford for a shape this rare. CI asserts `assets` with `verify.py --mode assets`; a native arm64 build is behaviourally equal but renumbers the English states.

wetext.how_picked: The repository carries no git tags and its VERSION file is a build-time placeholder (the release workflow writes `echo $version > VERSION`, so VERSION is 0.0.1 in every commit). The wheel's zip entries are stamped 2026-09-09 10:10 UTC, and c188fc7 is the last commit before that timestamp (10:05:56 UTC), five minutes earlier — the release ran on that tree. build_min.py is a transcription of that commit's build_fsts.py.
wetext.note: The wheel is `py3-none-any`: it ships no compiled code, only the FSTs and a kaldifst runtime. Nothing in it pins the toolchain, which is why the pynini/environment fields below matter as much as the commit.

wetextprocessing.how_picked: The wetext 0.1.8 release workflow did NOT pin this: it ran `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/wenet-e2e/WeTextProcessing.git`, so the pin is whatever master was on release day. There are no commits on that default branch between 039007e (2026-07-29) and 2026-10-31, so 039007e is the tree the release cloned. Confirmed empirically rather than assumed: building against 039007e on linux/amd64 reproduces all six shipped FSTs byte for byte. No other commit needed to be tried.
wetextprocessing.later_pins_in_that_repo: wetext's own release workflow (from 2026-11-05, i.e. 0.1.9 and later) pins c3b4d88d11c5efef817881f7e515cbdd3a19d99b. That is not this version and must not be used to rebuild 0.1.8.

pynini.how_picked: WeTextProcessing declares `pynini>=2.1.6` and the release did an unpinned `pip install -U`. PyPI's 2.1.7 uploaded 2025-09-04, a year before the 0.1.8 release, so resolution landed on 2.1.7. Using 2.1.7 reproduces the shipped bytes exactly.
pynini.distribution_that_reproduces_bytes: PyPI manylinux_2_28_x86_64 wheel (bundles its own OpenFst: pynini.libs/libfst.so.26)
pynini.distribution_that_does_not: conda-forge osx-arm64 build, linked against conda-forge openfst 1.8.4 — behaviourally identical, byte-different for English (see docs/superpowers/REPORT.md). Do not use it for CI byte-identity assertions.
pynini.version_string_gotcha: `pip show pynini` says 2.1.7, but `pynini.__version__` still reports "2.1.6.post1" — upstream did not bump the string in the 2.1.7 wheel. Judge the pin by the dist-info version, not by that attribute (verified 2026-11-15 in python:3.11-slim).

python.how_picked: wetext's release workflow sets `python-version: 3.11`. Verified with 3.11.18 (conda-forge) and python:3.11-slim (Docker).

environment.ci: linux/amd64, python:3.11-slim, pip install pynini==2.1.7, PYTHONPATH=<WeTextProcessing checkout>. See Dockerfile; ~19 s for all three languages under QEMU emulation on Apple Silicon with a 2 GiB memory cap.
environment.local_experiment: macOS arm64, conda-forge python 3.11 + pynini 2.1.7 (no PyPI wheel exists for osx-arm64). See docs/superpowers/env.md.

reproduction.compare: shasum -a 256 out/*/tn/*.fst  # compare with outputs.sha256 above
